evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Think deeply, execute quickly: speed and rigour, not speed or rigour.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Testing, data quality, observability, and governance are named as owned responsibilities throughout, and the explicit 'speed and rigour, not speed or rigour' framing signals rigour is not traded away for velocity.
evidence.domain_risk: Legal work is high-stake - it's regulated, complex, and deeply impactful
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The JD explicitly names the domain as regulated and high-stakes, with a dedicated governance/privacy responsibility around client personal data boundaries, giving high domain risk.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Our analytics stack is Snowflake for the warehouse, dbt Core for transformation, Fivetran for ingestion, GitHub Actions for CI and scheduling, Metabase for BI, and a Snowflake Cortex semantic layer
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A modern, fully-built stack with named tools throughout responsibilities and a semantic layer already shared across the team signals mid maturity, still growing ('consolidate rather than accumulate').
evidence.jd_authorship: Design and maintain dbt models, sources, tests and documentation across our layered architecture, and keep naming and structure coherent as it grows.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise tools, techniques, and a specific starting domain (product analytics: activation, feature adoption), giving a very clear picture of the actual work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: The analytics stack supports the whole business, so you would be working with Finance, Sales, Customer Success and Product rather than for any one of them.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role explicitly serves multiple stakeholder groups (Finance, Sales, Customer Success, Product) with genuinely equal weight and no single dominant audience, giving mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: What you would genuinely own is a domain, end to end: its models, its tests, its documentation, and the definitions behind its numbers.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strong ownership and direction-setting verbs dominate (own, define, design, consolidate rather than accumulate) with the explicit framing that requirement-following is a poor fit, giving strategic.
evidence.ai_role: We work in Claude Code day to day, alongside the usual editor and terminal.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is expected to use AI coding tools (Claude Code) as a normal daily part of the job for modelling, review and investigation, making this ai_user.
evidence.testing_framing: Extend our test suite, tune alerting so failures mean something, and keep the nightly pipeline honest.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and observability are named as an explicitly owned responsibility with action verbs (extend, tune, keep honest), not merely tools in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Keeping that boundary intact is a live decision every time we bring in a new source.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data governance and privacy boundaries are framed as an ongoing risk to manage, secondary to the primary modelling/ownership mission, consistent with moderate loss aversion.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Consolidate rather than accumulate. Extend and reshape what exists before adding to it, and retire what is no longer load-bearing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role explicitly blends greenfield work (shape how we measure a currently underserved domain) with consolidating and fixing the existing model estate, giving mixed.
evidence.loss_aversion: Keeping that boundary intact is a live decision every time we bring in a new source. — governance/privacy risk framed as an important but secondary concern.
